program.help:
Identify and remove the EMG component of a multichannel extracellular .dat using FastICA, on a per-probe basis, and write the EMG events out as if they were spikes.
C++ port of the algorithmic core of the labbox MATLAB EMG_removing toolbox (Chen 2019), restricted to the configuration the toolbox uses by default: deflation FastICA with the pow3 nonlinearity, run on high-pass filtered data, with the EMG component selected as the IC whose channel loading is most spatially uniform.
Per-probe semantics -------------------
Each probe declared in `probes:` is processed independently: FastICA runs on the union of that probe's anatomicalDescription channel groups (skip=0 channels only), producing one EMG mode per probe. All probes share a single output `<session>-emgclean.dat` — each probe writes only to its own channels, so the per-probe subtractions don't collide. Per-probe `.emg.<id>`, `.res.emg.<id>`, `.spk.emg.<id>` files use the probe's `id` field as the suffix.
If `probes:` is empty or absent, the wrapper falls back to one group per `spikeDetection.channelGroups` entry (legacy behaviour, 1-based suffixes).
Inputs ------ <session>.dat <session>.{xml,yaml,yml} (acquisitionSystem, probes, anatomicalDescription)
Outputs ------- <session>-emgclean.dat int16, same shape as .dat, EMG component subtracted (DC preserved; channels not in any probe pass through unchanged)
For each probe id `g`: <session>.emg.<g> int16 1-channel EMG_au trace (sample-rate-aligned) <session>.res.emg.<g> int64-LE event timestamps (sample indices) <session>.spk.emg.<g> int16 nSamples × nChannels per-event waveforms
<session>.emg.meta.yaml sidecar: per-probe loading (As), unmixing (Ws), uniformity score, FastICA iterations / convergence, threshold, channel mean
Pipeline --------
1. Pass 1 — for each probe, read up to idDuration seconds starting at idStart, demean per channel, apply 4th-order Butterworth high-pass at hpFreq, downsample by `downsample`, run FastICA deflation pow3 with K = max(round(0.8·nch), min(16, nch)). EMG component = column k of A maximising |sum( A[:,k] / ||A[:,k]|| )|. Threshold = thresholdFactor · 1.4826 · MAD(|EMG_au|) on the un-filtered subsample.
2. Pass 2 — stream the full .dat in chunks of `chunkSamples` samples per channel. For each sample compute EMG_au[t] = (raw[t,:] − μ) · Ws (per probe), then write clean[t,c] = raw[t,c] − As[c]·EMG_au[t] to <session>-emgclean.dat and EMG_au itself to <session>.emg.<g>.
3. Event detection — smooth |EMG_au| with a boxcar of envelopeWindowMs, find threshold-crossings separated by ≥ refractoryPeriod, refine each peak inside a peakSearchLength window.
4. Pass 3 — for each event timestamp, mmap the original .dat and extract a (nSamples × nChannels(probe)) int16 waveform window into <session>.spk.emg.<g>.
Parallelism -----------
Pass 1 FastICA is parallelised across probes via OpenMP (each thread runs an independent FastICA on its probe), and the FastICA pow3 inner kernel is OpenMP-parallel internally for the single-probe case. Pass 2 streaming subtraction is parallelised across probes per chunk (channel-disjoint writes). Pass 3 event detection + waveform extraction is parallelised across probes.
GPU acceleration of the FastICA pow3 inner kernel is available when the binary is built with `EXTRACTEMG_USE_CUDA=ON`, `EXTRACTEMG_USE_HIP=ON`, or `EXTRACTEMG_USE_SYCL=ON` (priority CUDA > HIP > SYCL). Selected at runtime via the `backend` parameter.
Run BEFORE ndm_hipass / ndm_extractspikes if you want spike detection to operate on the EMG-cleaned signal (use <session>-emgclean.dat as the source for downstream filtering — the wrapper does NOT rename .dat itself). Run AFTER spike detection if you want the .res.emg.<g> / .spk.emg.<g> events purely for analysis without disturbing the spike-extraction pipeline.
# hpFreq
High-pass cutoff in Hz applied during FastICA component identification (default 100). EMG dominates frequencies above the LFP corner; raising this above the LFP band biases the leading IC towards the muscle component.
# thresholdFactor
Event-detection threshold expressed as a multiple of the robust noise estimate 1.4826 · MAD(|EMG_au|). Default 5.0 — increase to capture only large bursts; lower to capture more low-amplitude EMG.
# envelopeWindowMs
Length of the boxcar smoothing window applied to |EMG_au| before peak detection (milliseconds). Default 20. Roughly the burst-fusion timescale.
# refractoryPeriod
Minimum number of samples between consecutive accepted events. Default 0 → derive from envelopeWindowMs.
# peakSearchLength
Number of samples after a threshold crossing within which the local maximum is found. Default 0 → use refractoryPeriod.
# downsample
Subsampling factor applied to the high-pass filtered identification data before FastICA. Default 3. Larger values trade ID accuracy for memory + speed.
# idStart, idDuration
Time window in seconds (relative to the start of .dat) over which FastICA observes the data to identify the EMG component. Default 0 + 60. 60 s is plenty for a stable EMG mode estimate; raise idDuration if the recording's EMG character changes substantially across long sessions.
# chunkSamples
Streaming chunk size for Pass 2 (samples per channel). Default 1048576 (= 1 MiB at int16, ≈ 32 s at 32 kHz × 16 channels).
# backend
Compute backend for the FastICA pow3 inner kernel. One of: `auto`, `cpu`, `cuda`, `hip`, `sycl`. Default `auto` selects in priority order CUDA > HIP > SYCL > CPU. Falls back to CPU at runtime if the requested backend was compiled out or no device is reachable. GPU backends skip device offload when N·nch < 100 000 samples (pow3 launch overhead would otherwise dominate).
# emgClean, emgTrace, emgWaveforms
`yes`/`no` toggles for each output. Default all yes. Set emgWaveforms=no for sessions where only the timestamps are needed; set emgClean=no during initial parameter tuning to avoid rewriting the cleaned dat.
